heading: INT. FAIRBANKS FAMILY DINING ROOM - EVENING

units.text: INT. FAIRBANKS FAMILY DINING ROOM - EVENING
A formal dining room in a house that is slightly too large.
A chandelier.
A mahogany table set for four, with a fifth chair pushed against the wall.
A grandfather clock ticks.
LAWRENCE FAIRBANKS-ODUYA (60s, three-piece suit, silver hair brushed back) carves a roast with exacting care.
At the other end of the table, MARGARET (60s, pearls, a smile on a timer) arranges napkins.
Between them sit their grown children: CLAUDIA (30s, tailored, a wedding ring she keeps turning) and THEODORE "TEDDY" (30s, a rumpled blazer, no tie).
The roast is placed.
Lawrence serves Claudia first, then Margaret, then himself.
Teddy's plate stays empty.
Claudia. Your promotion. Tell us.
units.name: LAWRENCE

units.text: It's nothing, Father. Just a title.
units.name: CLAUDIA

units.text: Don't undersell it.
units.name: LAWRENCE

units.text: Lawrence, let her eat.
units.name: MARGARET

units.text: Teddy takes a roll from the basket.
He tears it in half and lays both halves on his plate.
And you, Theodore?
units.name: LAWRENCE

units.text: I'm fine.
units.name: TEDDY

units.text: That wasn't the question.
units.name: LAWRENCE

units.text: It was an answer.
units.name: TEDDY

units.text: Margaret refills her water glass.
She does not drink.
Claudia glances at her brother; he glances back.
The clock ticks.
Your mother and I were discussing the lease.
units.name: LAWRENCE

units.text: What lease?
units.name: TEDDY

units.text: The office. Downtown. It expires in June.
units.name: LAWRENCE

units.text: I know when it expires.
units.name: TEDDY

units.text: Then you know we won't renew.
units.name: LAWRENCE

units.text: Teddy sets the roll down.
He wipes his fingers on the napkin, folds it into a neat square, and places it on the table.
Father, can we not do this tonight?
units.name: CLAUDIA

units.text: When, then?
units.name: LAWRENCE

units.text: More potatoes, anyone?
units.name: MARGARET

units.text: Thank you, Mother. No.
units.name: TEDDY

units.text: Lawrence sets down the knife and fork, side by side, at precisely five o'clock.
He looks at his son for a long, patient moment.
You've had five years.
units.name: LAWRENCE

units.text: I've had five years of you watching.
units.name: TEDDY

units.text: Claudia stands.
She begins clearing plates that have barely been touched.
Margaret rises, takes the potato dish, and goes to the kitchen without a word.
The door swings shut behind her.
Teddy pushes his chair back, takes his blazer from the chair, and stands there with it hanging from one hand.
Sit down.
units.name: LAWRENCE

units.text: No.
units.name: TEDDY

units.text: For the first time, Lawrence's hand trembles on the table.
He closes it into a fist and holds it there.
